articles.title: Astrocytic ablation of truncated TrkB receptors reduces amyloid plaques and prevents synaptic loss in 5xFAD mice
articles.content: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is essential for nervous system development and function and exerts its effects primarily through the tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB). The Ntrk2 gene encodes a full-length receptor (TrkB.FL) and two truncated isoforms (TrkB.T1 and TrkB.T2, collectively TrkB.T) that lack the intracellular tyrosine kinase domain. TrkB.T is expressed predominantly in astrocytes and is thought to inhibit BDNF-TrkB.FL signaling by sequestering BDNF and forming signaling-deficient heterodimers with TrkB.FL. Here, we investigated whether selective ablation of astrocytic TrkB.T could ameliorate Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology by enhancing endogenous BDNF-TrkB.FL signaling. Astrocyte-specific deletion of the Ntrk2 gene at 5 weeks of age reduced cortical TrkB.T expression by more than 80% without affecting TrkB.FL levels. TrkB.T ablation increased the size of Bassoon-positive presynaptic active zones, consistent with enhanced BDNF-TrkB.FL signaling. Remarkably, astrocytic TrkB.T ablation reduced {beta}-amyloid plaque burden by more than 60% in the cortex, hippocampus, and subiculum of 6-month-old 5xFAD mice, despite having no detectable effect on microgliosis or astrogliosis. Furthermore, TrkB.T ablation prevented reductions in the density and size of PSD-95-positive postsynaptic sites in the cortex and hippocampus of 5xFAD mice at 1 year old. Together, these findings identify astrocytic TrkB.T as an important regulator of amyloid pathology and synaptic integrity in an AD mouse model. Our results suggest that selectively reducing TrkB.T expression represents a promising therapeutic strategy to enhance endogenous neuroprotective BDNF-TrkB.FL signaling, reduce amyloid pathology, and preserve synaptic integrity in AD.

SIK3 controls synaptic localization of NMDA receptors by phosphorylating GluN1
articles.content:
Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02469-9

SIK3 kinase controls synaptic NMDA receptor recruitment by phosphorylating GluN1 at a single site. Loss or inhibition of SIK3 markedly reduces synaptic NMDARs, while a gain-of-function mutation increases GluN1 phosphorylation and NMDAR levels.

articles.title: A corticohypothalamic circuit that mediates maternal awakening to pup cries
articles.content:
Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02458-y

Tang, Wu et al. identify a brain circuit that enables mother mice to wake selectively to pup cries. Motherhood strengthens this pathway through increased dopamine receptor D1 expression, helping mothers to be responsive to offspring during sleep.

articles.title: Computational approaches to deep learning–driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review
articles.content: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a widely used non-invasive neurophysiological technique for analyzing brain dynamics and diagnosing neurological diseases. However, the non-stationary nature, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability of EEG signals cause significant challenges to traditional analytical approaches. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful computational tool for EEG analysis, which enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy with minimal human-driven feature extraction. This review systematically explains computational approaches in deep learning-driven EEG analysis for the diagnosis of neurological diseases. It includes recent advances in deep learning architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), hybrid configurations, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), Large Language Models (LLM), autoencoders, and transformer-based models, with a focus on their capacity to model spatial, temporal, and spatiotemporal dynamics in EEG signals. This is applicable in diagnosing major neurological disorders such as Epilepsy, Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Encephalopathy, Parkinson’s disease (PD), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), sleep disorders, and developmental brain disorders. Furthermore, we discuss essential preprocessing strategies and denoising techniques, showing how removing biological artifacts prevents diagnostic models from confusing noise with actual signs of disease. Key challenges such as limited data availability, lack of model interpretability, inter-subject variability, and difficulty in clinical translation are identified and critically discussed. Finally, key emerging trends and future research directions are identified to support the development of clinical applications of EEG-based disease diagnostic systems.

articles.title: Wave-function formalism for evolving neural dynamics: a mathematical framework informed by EEG
articles.content: The organization of distributed neural activity remains one of the central challenges in computational neuroscience. Contemporary frameworks, including Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory, entropy-based approaches, and electromagnetic field theories, have advanced our understanding of neural coordination but employ different mathematical descriptions of large-scale brain dynamics. This study investigates whether wave-function formalism provides a useful mathematical framework for representing evolving neural dynamics measured using electroencephalography (EEG). Rather than introducing a new electrophysiological measure or proposing a new mechanism of consciousness, the framework represents complementary EEG observables within a common state-space description of neural activity. Mathematical inspiration is drawn from Everett’s representation of evolving state spaces, although no claims are made regarding quantum computation or quantum processes in the brain. Electroencephalographic recordings from interictal, preictal, and ictal seizure states (150 EEG segments) were analyzed using complementary measures of signal amplitude, spectral organization, entropy, phase dynamics, cross-frequency coupling, and recurrence quantification. Statistical comparisons employed nonparametric analyses, effect-size estimation, confidence intervals, and post hoc testing. Significant differences were observed across all major electrophysiological domains. Ictal recordings exhibited increased signal amplitude, redistribution of spectral power toward lower frequencies, reduced entropy, altered phase organization, changes in cross-frequency coupling, and increased recurrence structure, indicating coordinated changes in evolving neural dynamics during seizure progression. These findings are interpreted within a mathematical framework that treats established EEG observables as complementary descriptors of a single evolving neural state. The principal contribution of this work is the proposal of a mathematically grounded and experimentally testable representation of evolving neural dynamics. Whether this formalism provides new insight into cognition or conscious experience remains an empirical question for future investigation.

articles.title: Implementing the ILAE 2025 seizure taxonomy in medical software
articles.content: The International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE), working via a multidisciplinary task force, has issued a position paper with updated seizure classification guidelines (2025) replacing its previous guidance (2017), establishing a revised de-facto standard for clinical assessment and classification of epileptic seizures. The 2025 model simplifies the system, making it easier to adopt in different clinical settings while also clarifying the taxonomic rules, the definition of consciousness, and the application of phenomena-based descriptors. As a result, clinical practitioners, technologists, and medical software developers also face the challenge of adopting the new standard in their applications and workflows. To aid in the realization of this update in medical device software, this article presents a proposed numerical structure for ILAE 2025 edition of the seizure classification system as a definition of interacting bitfields, establishing an open reference implementation to support common storage and interoperability between software environments. Assigning each orthogonal concept to a single bit, we encode the core ontology and expanded descriptor set so that they fit into 32-bit and 128-bit unsigned integers, respectively. TypeScript, known for its expressiveness and practical applicability, is used as the implementation language for these definitions. Examples are provided to help implementers incorporate the proposed specification into their software, as well guidance for mapping from the ILAE 2017 type system to the updated ILAE 2025 type system. The reference specification, with test cases and examples, is maintained in a public code repository and available under a permissive license.

articles.title: Generative-augmented multimodal neuroaffective decoding for product evaluation: toward neurofeedback-driven human-in-the-loop co-design
articles.content: BackgroundKansei engineering traditionally relies on self-reported evaluations of product impressions, which are susceptible to contextual influences, recall bias, and assessment timing. Multimodal psychophysiological measurements offer complementary insights into affective responses, but integrating heterogeneous signals with limited sample sizes remains challenging. This study proposes Generative-Augmented Multimodal Affective Fusion (GAMAF) to predict perceived attractiveness, innovativeness, and friendliness in product evaluation.MethodsGAMAF integrates feature-space conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial learning with gradient penalty (cWGAN-GP), cross-modal attention, graph-based interactions, and adaptive modality weighting. Fifty participants evaluated three automobile cockpit designs, yielding 150 participant–stimulus trials after multimodal quality control. Electroencephalography (EEG), eye tracking (ET), and peripheral physiological signals were integrated and evaluated using nested participant-wise cross-validation.ResultsGAMAF achieved mean outer-fold R² values of 0.810, 0.850, and 0.840 for attractiveness, innovativeness, and friendliness, respectively, each with a standard deviation of 0.016. These values exceeded those of the Multimodal Transformer baseline (0.75, 0.78, and 0.76, respectively). Across the three targets, GAMAF reduced aggregate mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) by approximately 29.6% and 29.7%, respectively. Ablation analyses supported the integrated architecture, while adaptive modality weights revealed target-dependent patterns.DiscussionGAMAF demonstrates the potential of generative-augmented multimodal fusion for decoding Kansei-related product impressions. However, performance comparisons remain descriptive because baseline variability and participant-level uncertainty were not quantified. Further validation on unseen product designs and closed-loop design optimization is needed to establish its generalizability and practical utility.
